info.title: StagingPro V2 Migration API (BigCommerce)
info.description:
Control-plane REST API for the StagingPro V2 BC Migration engine. Register stores, map storefront channels, launch and control migrations, read live progress, and query the cross-migration knowledge base.

> **Placeholder notice** — this reference is scaffolded from the V2 control-plane routes. Base URLs, examples, and field notes will be finalised as the public surface is confirmed.

servers.description: StagingPro V2 control plane (behind the VortexIQ platform proxy)

host.description: Placeholder host — replace with your StagingPro V2 deployment host.

tags.name: Stores
tags.description: Connected Stores registry — saved BigCommerce store credentials (tokens are held server-side and never returned).

tags.name: Channel Mapping
tags.description: Per store-pair source→destination storefront (channel) mapping, saved and reused across migrations.

tags.name: Migrations
tags.description: Create migrations, list history, and read live run detail.

tags.name: Migration Controls
tags.description: Pause, resume, cancel, and verify-only re-runs.

tags.name: Counts & Forecast
tags.description: Fast source-store entity counts and pre-launch sizing/ETA forecasts. No run is created.

tags.name: Fix Runs
tags.description: VortexSpace Track B — two-phase (plan → approve → execute) fix runs dispatched from audit findings.

tags.name: Ask Viq
tags.description: Streamed migration-support assistant scoped to this host's runs.

tags.name: Knowledge Base
tags.description: Support-only: learned failure patterns, structural known issues, and manual learning notes. Requires X-Support-Key.

tags.name: Support Diagnostics
tags.description: Support-only: full run state, watchdog oversight, and progress logs. Requires X-Support-Key.

get.description: Liveness probe. The only endpoint that does not require `X-Proxy-Key`.

runnerMode.description: Active execution mode for migration runs.

get.description: Returns every saved store in the Connected Stores registry. API tokens are never included — `tokenSet` indicates whether one is held server-side.

post.description: Registers a BigCommerce store with its API token. The store's real name is pulled from BigCommerce automatically (best-effort). Optional WebDAV credentials enable Page Builder widget-image migration.

patch.description: Partially updates a saved store. Supplying a new `token` re-fetches the store name from BigCommerce.

delete.description: Removes a store from the registry. Idempotent — deleting an unknown id still returns `ok`.

get.description: Fetches the storefront channels of a saved store live from BigCommerce (used by the V2 channel dropdowns and multi-storefront mapping).
Returns the saved source→destination storefront (channel) mapping for a store pair. Empty when no mapping has been saved yet.

put.description: Saves (replaces) the channel mapping for a store pair. A pair with `destination_channel_id: null` is unmapped — its channel assignments are dropped during migration. Migrating **all storefronts** requires a saved mapping.

post.description:
Queues a migration. Two request forms are accepted:

- **By saved stores** — reference registry store ids; credentials are resolved server-side. This is the form the StagingPro UI uses.
- **By raw credentials** — pass `store_hash` + `token` per side directly (programmatic/legacy path). Only this form supports `selection` and `theme_activation`.

Guards enforced at this boundary:
- source and destination must be different stores
- a store labelled **Production** in the registry can never be a destination
- migrating **all storefronts** requires a saved channel mapping
- selecting `orders`, `customers`, or `gift_certificates` requires `anonymise_customer_data: true`
- every `theme_activation` key must appear in `selection.themes`, and no destination channel may be targeted twice
- every `selection.page_template_globals` entry must appear in `selection.page_templates`

selectivePicks.summary: Selective migration (picked ids, themes, page templates)

400.description: Validation or guard failure. `error` is one of `invalid_request`, `store_not_found`, `channel_mapping_required`, `production_destination_refused`, `anonymise_required`.

get.description: Migration history, newest first. Fix runs (Track B) are excluded by default — pass `task_kind=fix` to query the fix lane.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only runs created on/after this date (ISO).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only runs created on/before this date (ISO).

get.description: Customer-facing run detail. While the run directory exists this is the **live** engine state; after teardown it is served from the durable final-state snapshot.

Per-item issue log: failed items and intentionally skipped items (with the human-readable reason). Sanitised — entity/name/status/reason only, never request bodies or credentials. Capped at the most recent 500 per list.

skipped.name: Legacy landing
skipped.reason: page type not supported by destination theme

get.description: Content-fidelity comparison report for the run. Served from the run directory while it exists; returns `no_report` after teardown.

200.description: Fidelity report (shape defined by the engine's fidelity module).

404.description: Run not found, or no fidelity report exists for this run (`no_report`).

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream of live run state. Emits an initial `state` event immediately, `state` events on every engine update, and a final one-shot `end` event when the run reaches a terminal status (already-terminal runs receive `end` immediately). Keep-alive comment pings are sent every 15 seconds.

200.description: SSE stream (`text/event-stream`). `state` events carry a `MigrationDetail` JSON payload.

post.description: Pauses an active run. The engine checkpoints its state; a paused run can be resumed at any time.

Re-queues a paused or interrupted run. The run resumes from its checkpoint (the id-map in the run directory), which also makes resume the only guard-safe way to re-run against an already-populated destination.

If run tokens were wiped after completion, they are re-injected from the stores registry; when the stores are no longer registered the call fails with `tokens_unavailable`.

409.description: Run tokens were wiped and the stores are not in the registry (`tokens_unavailable`).

post.description: Cancels a queued or active run. Cancellation is a control-plane decision and is authoritative over the engine's last written state.

Re-runs a completed migration in **verify** mode: read-only source/destination comparison, no writes. Requires the run directory (and its config) to still exist, and valid tokens (re-injected from the registry when wiped).

409.description: `config_unavailable` (run dir cleaned up) or `tokens_unavailable` (tokens wiped and stores unregistered).

post.description:
Fast, direct, parallel reads of the **source** store's entity totals for the selected entity keys. No engine container is launched, no run is recorded. Accepts a saved source store id or raw source credentials — the destination is never touched.

Pass a `selection` to scope the counts to a selective run's real picks (products, categories, pages, promotions), so the returned badges match what that run would actually migrate rather than the whole store. Orders are counted per selected `order_status_{id}` when those keys are requested.

200.description: Entity counts. Keys listed in `estimated` are sample/probe estimates rather than exact totals.

502.description: Counts could not be fetched from BigCommerce (`counts_failed`).

post.description:
Pre-launch sizing and ETA forecast for the selected entities: recommended container memory/CPU tier plus estimated total wall-clock. Uses the same forecaster as migration kickoff, so the numbers match what a real run would be sized with.

The forecast is **run-scoped**:
- `selection` scopes the counts the ETA is priced from - a 10-of-10,000 product pick is no longer forecast as a whole-store run
- `conflict_strategy` prices the extra work `update`/`replace` imply (destination prefetch, per-matched reconcile, and for `replace` a prune pass)
- orders are priced on the selected `order_status_{id}` counts rather than the all-statuses total

Memory sizing stays pinned to store scale regardless of the picks - see the `memMB` note on the response schema. Calling this with source credentials only (no destination) means `update`/`replace` degrade to an assume-all-matched basis.

502.description: Forecast could not be computed from BigCommerce (`forecast_failed`).

post.description:
VortexSpace Track B. Dispatches a **fix run** for an audit finding, in two phases:

- `phase: "plan"` (default) — provisions a fresh run sized by `affected_count` and returns `201` with the new `request_id`.
- `phase: "execute"` — re-arms the **same** run directory after merchant approval and returns `202`. Fails with `run_dir_expired` when the plan run dir was reclaimed.

Results flow back to the platform via the fix mirror callback.

202.description: Execute phase re-queued on the existing run.

409.description: Plan run dir was reclaimed — re-run plan (`run_dir_expired`).

get.description:
Streams a Viq migration-support session as Server-Sent Events. Viq answers with live host context (run history, active engine containers) and is read-only by policy — it diagnoses, it never mutates.

Pass `new=1` on the first call of a session, then reuse the same `session` id to continue it.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Session id (alphanumeric and dashes). Reuse to continue a conversation.

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: Set to `1` to start a new session with the support system prompt.

200.description: SSE stream of assistant output lines (`data:` events), followed by a final `done` event.

get.description: The folded cross-migration knowledge base: every learned error fingerprint with its best-known resolution and success rate.
The engineering queue: structural engine bugs auto-heal can't fix (they need a code change). Open issues only by default; pass `all=1` to include resolved ones.

post.description: Records a manual diagnosis into the knowledge base (same vocabulary as automatic auto-heal diagnoses) and mirrors it to the shared learning store immediately. Use `resolution` for heal advice and `known_issue` only for structural engine bugs.

fp.description: The error fingerprint the note was filed under.

post.description: Marks a structural known issue resolved once its engine fix has shipped, which stops the recognition short-circuit on future runs.

parameters.name: fp
parameters.description: The error fingerprint of the known issue.

note.description: Optional resolution note (e.g. the fixing commit).

post.description: **Internal.** Dispatches the on-host AI engineer against a structural engine bug: it clones the platform repo (sparse), produces a minimal fix, verifies it compiles, and opens a pull request on a `viq-fix/*` branch. It can never push to the base branch. Fire-and-forget — the PR appearing on GitHub is the success signal.

branch.description: The `viq-fix/*` branch the fix will be pushed to.

get.description: Combined support view for one run: full engine state **including load telemetry**, watchdog oversight (escalation + diagnosis decision), and the progress-log tail.
Watchdog escalation and the auto-heal diagnosis decision for one run, when present.
Tail of the run's `progress.log` as plain text.

VortexSpace Track B: the live **crew activity** log for a fix run, served as newline-delimited JSON (`fix_activity.jsonl`, one JSON object per line). Each line is an event emitted by the fix crew as the run proceeds, so polling this endpoint gives a per-event view of what the fix is doing.

Returns an empty body for runs that produced no activity log (any migration run, or a fix run whose directory was reclaimed).

proxyKey.name: X-Proxy-Key
proxyKey.description: Edge key required on every `/api/*` call except `/api/health`. Injected automatically by the VortexIQ platform proxy; required explicitly when calling the control plane directly.

supportKey.name: X-Support-Key
supportKey.description: Support key required on Knowledge Base and Support Diagnostics endpoints (may also be passed as `?key=`).

MigrationId.name: id
MigrationId.description: The migration request id (uppercase UUID) returned by Create migration.

StoreId.name: id
StoreId.description: The saved store id from the Connected Stores registry.

OrgId.name: X-Org-Id
OrgId.description: Organisation context, injected by the VortexIQ platform proxy. When present, runs are scoped to that org — a run belonging to another org returns 404.

InvalidRequest.description: Request failed validation (`invalid_request`). `details` carries field-level errors.

NotFound.description: Resource not found — or belongs to a different organisation (`not_found`).

details.description: Field-level validation details, present when `error` is `invalid_request`.

Store.description: A saved store in the Connected Stores registry. Tokens are held server-side and never returned.

environmentType.description: Label such as `Production`, `Staging`, `UAT-1`. Empty when unlabelled. A store labelled Production can never be a migration destination.

storeName.description: Real store name pulled from BigCommerce.

tokenSet.description: Whether an API token is held server-side.

webdavSet.description: Whether WebDAV credentials are present (needed for widget-image migration).

token.description: BigCommerce API account token. Stored server-side, never returned.

b2b.description: Mark as a B2B Edition store.

webdav_username.description: Optional WebDAV username (Settings → File Access) — needed only to migrate Page Builder widget images.

token.description: Supplying a new token re-fetches the store name from BigCommerce.

destination_channel_id.description: `null` = unmapped; the source channel's assignments are dropped.

Selection.description: Selective migration: per-entity source picks. Parents/ancestors are auto-included; products auto-pull their brands and categories. A selection also scopes [entity counts](/vortex-apps/staging-pro/api/get-entity-counts) and the [forecast](/vortex-apps/staging-pro/api/get-forecast), so a 10-of-10,000 pick is not sized as a whole-store run.

themes.description: Selective theme migration. Themes are picked by **UUID** (BigCommerce theme ids are uuids, not integers). When present, the bulk `activate_theme` boolean is ignored in favour of `theme_activation`.

page_templates.description: Selective page templates: `template_file` values (all begin `pages/`, e.g. `pages/home`). Template-LEVEL Page Builder content only - entity-scoped contexts (a specific product/category/page) are not included.

page_template_globals.description: Page templates whose **global** widget content also migrates. Must be a subset of `page_templates` - an entry not present there is rejected.

ThemeActivation.description:
Selective themes only: destination channel ids to **activate** each picked theme on, keyed by source theme uuid. Absent or empty = migrate-only (upload without activating).

Two rules are enforced:
- every key must appear in `selection.themes`
- a destination channel may be targeted by **at most one** theme activation (a storefront channel has exactly one active theme)

destination_store_id.description: Saved destination store id. Must not be labelled Production.

source_channel_id.description: Channel-specific mode: the one source storefront to migrate from. Omit (with `destination_channel_id`) for all-storefronts mode, which requires a saved channel mapping.

destination_channel_id.description: Channel-specific mode: the destination storefront to map onto.

auto_heal.description: Allow the watchdog + diagnoser to auto-recover failed items. Default true.

channel_scoped_products.description: Migrate only products assigned to `source_channel_id` (else migrate all products and assign them to the mapped destination channel).

activate_theme.description: Activate the migrated theme on the destination (else upload only).

conflict_strategy.description: How an entity that already exists on the destination is handled: `skip` = leave as-is (default), `update` = diff-gated additive update, `replace` = update plus prune destination-only items.

destination.description: Must be a different store than the source.

source_storefront.description: Source storefront (channel) name, for history display.

destination_storefront.description: Destination storefront (channel) name, for history display.

channel_map.description: Source channel id → destination channel id map.

channel_scope.description: Restrict the whole run to this one source channel (set together with a single-pair `channel_map`).

forecast.description: Pre-launch sizing forecast (engine-docker mode with forecasting enabled); `null` otherwise.

MigrationSummary.description: One row in the migration history list.

selective.description: True when the run used a specific-id selection (Selective vs Bulk).

MigrationStatus.description: `pending_approval` is a fix-run-only resting status after the plan phase.

matched.description: Already in sync with the source — examined, no write needed (update/replace).

widgets.description: Page widgets only: widget nodes landed on the destination (inside published trees plus classic placements created). Contexts are the work unit; widgets are the content unit.

MigrationState.description: The live run state the engine keeps continuously updated.

etaSeconds.description: Per-phase remaining estimate written by the engine.

overallEtaSeconds.description: Whole-run ETA from the forecast, live-calibrated by observed destination latency.

warnings.description: Non-blocking issues (e.g. unrecoverable 404 source images) — they do not fail the run.

Forecast.description:
Pre-launch sizing and ETA estimate derived from the source store's entity counts.

Sizing and ETA are priced from **different bases on purpose**: the ETA follows the run's real scope (selective picks, conflict strategy, selected order statuses), while memory is pinned to **store scale** - the engine's variant and id-map residents do not shrink with a small pick, so sizing on picked counts alone would under-provision the container.

counts.description: Per-selected-entity counts (the basis for sizing and ETA). Scoped by `selection` when one was supplied.

estimated.description: Count keys that are sample/probe estimates rather than exact totals.

memMB.description: Recommended container memory (MiB). Pinned to store scale, not to the picked subset.

etaAssumedRttMs.description: The blended destination op-latency the ETA assumed - the live ETA is calibrated against this.

etaAssumedMs.description: Per-op-class latencies (ms) the ETA assumed. The engine compares read-against-read and write-against-write, so heavy creates are not judged against a blended baseline.

strategy.description: The conflict strategy the ETA was priced with (absent = create-only). `update` and `replace` add destination-prefetch and per-matched reconcile terms; `replace` adds a prune term.

destProducts.description: Destination catalogue size at kickoff. Absent or `0` when unknown - the source-only forecast button has no destination credentials, so it assumes all-matched.

basis.description: `fallback` = counts unavailable; `fix` = sized by affected-item count.

affected.description: Fix runs only: the affected-item count sizing was derived from.

status.description: HTTP status of the failing call, when applicable.

reason.description: Truncated error body or human-readable skip reason.

source_store_id.description: Saved source store id. Counts read only the source store.

conflict_strategy.description: Forecast only: price the ETA for this destination conflict strategy. Ignored by entity counts.

channel_map.description: Optional channel map (used by the forecast's per-channel sizing).

conflict_strategy.description: Forecast only: price the ETA for this destination conflict strategy. Ignored by entity counts.

counts.description: Entity key → total on the source store.

estimated.description: Keys whose value is a sample/probe estimate (not an exact count).

request_id.description: Execute phase only: the plan run's request id to re-arm.

fix.description: The fix block for the finding being remediated. Forward-compatible — the fix engine defines additional fields.

execution_id.description: Platform audit execution id (correlates the result callback).

affected_count.description: Affected item count — sizes the fix container.

platform.description: Which write API the fix targets (e.g. `bigcommerce`).

token.description: Platform write token — lives only in the run directory.

ok.description: Whether the runner accepted the control action.

KbEntry.description: Folded knowledge for one error fingerprint, aggregated across all migrations.

knownIssue.description: Present when classed as a structural engine bug.

KnownIssue.description: A structural engine bug needing a code fix (not auto-healable).

suggestedFix.description: One line naming the engine code change that would fix it.

type.description: `resolution` = heal advice; `known_issue` = structural engine bug only.

entity.description: Entity key the failure occurred on.

suggestedFix.description: Known issues: one-line suggested engine fix.

requestId.description: The run this was observed on.

body.description: The fix brief the AI engineer works from.

github_token.description: Short-lived GitHub token passed per-call; never stored.

ClaudeDecision.description: The auto-heal diagnoser's decision on an escalated run.

remediate.description: Declarative payload transforms the engine validates and applies on retry.
